done.why: I'd had a complete little episode (the duel and the unmasking) and stopped there, having seen only a small part of the place.

about: A dreamlike cave world where you are being tested by an old silver-haired man. You explore dark passages with a lantern, find a sword, and face a shadow double of yourself.

moments.note: Moving south into the dark warned about a grue; the lantern fixed it.
Trying to pull the sword gave a joke: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
Going west said the mist turned me back, and I wasn't sure why.
Asking who was there got 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.'
The sword appeared in my hand, glowing, when the hooded figure showed up.

wished: To ask the footsteps who was there
A hint about whether to spare or finish the figure
To know my health during the fight

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
lines.why: Funny, and it showed the world has a voice.

fun.why: The fight and the reveal were satisfying, and the jokes landed.

engagement.why: I wanted to find out who the figure was and followed the wounded-figure cues.

difficulty.why: The fight was straightforward and nothing blocked me for long.

interestingness.why: The dream frame and the shadow double are intriguing.

prose.why: Evocative and economical. The combat text was varied.
